newsitem.title: USA: Motorola sees slow rebound for phone market share.
newsitem.headline: Motorola sees slow rebound for phone market share.

text.p: Motorola Inc said Friday a recovery in its wireless phone market share will "take some time" despite posted improvements in the sector in the fourth quarter.

"It's important to remind everyone that the handset market...has become a very competitive one over the past year or so," Ed Gams, the head of investor relations, told analysts on a conference call. "A recovery in market share by us is going to not come easy, and it will take some time," he said.
Gams said it is too early to speculate on Motorola's fourth quarter market share.

Analysts, however, have estimated Motorola's current market share in mobile phones at about 38 percent -- a share that is considered high in the industry but has declined. In 1995 it was estimated at about 45 percent.
Motorola said its new wireless phones, including Global System for Mobile communications (GSM) handsets and its StarTAC wearable phone, have been well-received in the market.
In fact, Gams said some of the new GSM products had demand which exceeded the company's ability to supply.
"We're going to ramp volumes up, but a quick snap back in market share probably isn't going to happen," Gams said.
Motorola said the shift to digital phones, especially in the United States where mainly analog technology is used, may also give market share a boost.
Digital phones accounted for 42 percent of handset sales in the fourth quarter, and 37 percent for the full year 1996, the company said. In 1995, digital phones were 35 percent of the total.
Jeff Stoner, manager of investor relations, said the company does not think it lost market share in the United States in 1996, but business in Japan was slow and a quick turnaround is not expected.
"As the U.S. shifts to digital, we expect that some of the new products we're launching are going to leave us in a very strong market position in the U.S.," Stoner said.

Late Thursday, Motorola reported fourth quarter sales in its General Systems Segment rose 17 percent to $3.3 billion and orders were up 21 percent versus last year. The segment includes cellular phones, which the company said also posted increased orders.
